title: The Truth About Buying Organic Food
summary: Explains what the organic label requires and concludes there is no evidence organic food is healthier, with mixed environmental trade-offs.

assertions.quote: there is no evidence that organic food has more nutrients or is better for you in any way
So far, there's no evidence that organic foods are healthier, as many people claim.
organic food usually comes back with fewer than conventional crops
Virtually all foods are still within the EPA's safety limits for pesticides, no matter how they're produced
organic certification requires farmers to grow crops without chemical fertilizers and to use a limited number of pesticides
Cows and other ruminants that naturally eat grass have to be able to graze for at least a third of the year
organic farms aren't as productive as conventional farms
it takes about 25% more farmland to grow organic food than to grow the same amount of regular food
Some research also suggests organic farming can support more biodiversity
You shouldn't buy it because it's healthier or tastier, that much is clear.
In this case, the organics label prevents a sustainable farming practice, which is kind of a waste.

verdicts.note: Organic rules ban irradiation, biosolids and GE crops, which have food-safety or environmental benefits in some uses, though each has trade-offs.

The ban on mineral fertilisers excludes selenium-fortified N fertiliser and may partly explain lower selenium in organic milk; authors suggest revising organic mineral rules, a nutritional rather than safety example.

assertions.quote: In terms of preventing food poisoning, organic food also seems to match conventional food.
